ei.title: Why Moving Is Stressful for Children
ei.subject: 9월_2023 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Why Moving Is Stressful for Children

fullPassage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.

questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly (A)[stressful / relaxing] for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly (B)[ignored / affected] by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of (C)[community / isolation], which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① relaxing(느긋하게 하는): 이사가 아이들에게 '느긋한' 일이라는 것은 뒤 내용과 모순된다.
❌ ② ignored(무시된): 어린 아이들이 이사에 '무시된다'는 문맥은 어색하다. 이사의 '영향을 받는다'가 맞다.
✅ ③ stressful(스트레스가 되는) — affected(영향을 받는) — community(공동체): 모두 원문 그대로의 단어이다.
❌ ④ isolation(고립): 배경을 나누는 것은 '고립'이 아니라 '공동체' 의식 형성에 기여한다.
det.tip: stressful ↔ relaxing, affected ↔ ignored, community ↔ isolation.

questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel (A)[disoriented / confident] when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite (B)[figurative / literal], and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a (C)[balance / chaos] between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① disoriented(혼란스러운) — literal(문자 그대로의) — balance(균형): 모두 원문 그대로의 단어이다.
❌ ② confident(자신 있는): 일상이 무너질 때 '자신 있게' 느낀다는 것은 문맥에 어긋난다.
❌ ③ figurative(비유적인): 어린 아이의 이해는 '비유적'이 아니라 '문자 그대로'라 미리 상상하기 어렵다.
❌ ④ chaos(혼돈): 과거 인정과 적응 돕기 사이에 세워야 할 것은 '혼돈'이 아니라 '균형'이다.
det.tip: disoriented ↔ confident, literal ↔ figurative, balance ↔ chaos.

questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is (A)[disrupted / maintained] and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them (B)[resist / adjust] to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is (C)[essential / optional] for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① maintained(유지되는): 일상이 '유지되면' 혼란을 느낄 이유가 없으므로 문맥에 맞지 않는다.
❌ ② resist(저항하다): 아이들이 새 장소에 '저항하도록' 돕는 것이 아니라 '적응하도록' 돕는다.
❌ ③ optional(선택적인): 공동체 의식은 모든 아이에게 '선택'이 아니라 '필수적'이다.
✅ ④ disrupted(무너지는) — adjust(적응하다) — essential(필수적인): 모두 원문 그대로의 단어이다.
det.tip: disrupted ↔ maintained, adjust ↔ resist, essential ↔ optional.

questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly ①<u>stressful</u> for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is ②<u>familiar</u> is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly ③<u>affected</u> by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is ④<u>unnecessary</u> for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ④ unnecessary(불필요한): 공동체 의식은 모든 아이, 특히 전환기의 아이들에게 '필수적(essential)'이다. '불필요하다'는 정반대라 부적절하다.
✅ ① stressful(스트레스가 되는): 이사가 아이들에게 스트레스가 된다는 문맥에 적절하다.
✅ ② familiar(친숙한): 친숙한 모든 것이 사라진다는 문맥에 적절하다.
✅ ③ affected(영향을 받는): 어린 아이들이 이사의 영향을 받는다는 문맥에 적절하다.
det.tip: essential(필수적인) ↔ unnecessary(불필요한). 공동체 의식은 필수.

questions.passage: While moving is ①<u>easy</u> for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of ②<u>security</u> and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their ③<u>understanding</u> at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a ④<u>balance</u> between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① easy(쉬운): 이사가 모두에게 '쉽다'면 아이들에게 특히 스트레스가 된다는 흐름과 모순된다. '어렵다(difficult)'가 맞다.
✅ ② security(안정감): 아이들이 안정감을 잃는다는 문맥에 적절하다.
✅ ③ understanding(이해): 이 시기 아이들의 이해가 문자 그대로라는 문맥에 적절하다.
✅ ④ balance(균형): 과거를 인정하는 것과 적응을 돕는 것 사이의 균형이라는 문맥에 적절하다.
det.tip: difficult(어려운) ↔ easy(쉬운). 이사는 모두에게 어려운 일.

questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel ①<u>disoriented</u> when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite ②<u>literal</u>, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to ③<u>avoid</u> a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of ④<u>community</u>, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ③ avoid(피하다): 과거 인정과 적응 돕기 사이의 균형을 '피하는' 것이 아니라 '확립(establish)'하는 것이 중요하다.
✅ ① disoriented(혼란스러운): 일상이 무너질 때 혼란을 느낀다는 문맥에 적절하다.
✅ ② literal(문자 그대로의): 이 시기 아이들의 이해 방식으로 적절하다.
✅ ④ community(공동체): 공동체 의식을 세운다는 문맥에 적절하다.
det.tip: establish(확립하다) ↔ avoid(피하다). 균형을 확립하는 것이 중요.

❌ ④ organized(정리된): 일상이 '정리되면' 오히려 안정되므로 혼란과 모순된다.

questions.passage:
(A) They will move to a quiet <u>place</u> next month, far from their old neighborhood.

(B) Please <u>place</u> your books on the shelf before you leave the classroom.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 place의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) place = 장소(조용한 장소로 이사 간다), (B) place = 놓다(책을 선반에 놓다)
det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) 장소 — (B) 놓다: (A)의 place는 이사 갈 '장소'를 뜻하는 명사, (B)의 place는 책을 '놓다'라는 동사로 각각 적절하다.
❌ ① (A) 놓다 — (B) 장소: (A)에서 place는 명사 '장소'이지 동사 '놓다'가 아니다.
❌ ③ (A) 장소 — (B) 순위를 매기다: (B)는 물건을 선반에 '놓다'이지 순위와 무관하다.
❌ ④ (A) 직장 — (B) 놓다: (A)의 place는 이사 갈 장소이지 '직장'이 아니다.
det.tip: place는 다의어: (명사) 장소, (동사) 놓다/두다, (동사) 순위를 매기다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another"

det.korean: 한 상태에서 다른 상태로 변해 가는 과정이나 시기 → transition(전환)
det.analysis:
❌ ① balance(균형): 두 대상 사이의 안정 상태를 뜻하며 '변화 과정'이 아니다.
✅ ② transition(전환): 한 상태에서 다른 상태로 바뀌는 과정을 뜻하는 정의에 정확히 부합한다.
❌ ③ security(안정감): 안전하다는 느낌으로 '변화'와 무관하다.
❌ ④ routine(일상): 반복되는 일과로 정의와 맞지 않는다.
det.tip: transition = 전환/이행. 한 상태에서 다른 상태로 넘어가는 과정.

questions.passage: It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and __________ (focus) on helping them adjust to the new place.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: focus → focusing. between A and B 구조에서 앞의 validating과 병렬을 이루는 동명사 형태가 필요하다.
det.analysis: focus → focusing. 'between validating ... and __________'에서 and 앞의 validating(동명사)과 짝을 이루도록 뒤에도 동명사 focusing이 와야 한다. between A and B는 A와 B의 형태가 같아야 하는 병렬 구조이다.
det.tip: 병렬 구조: between validating ... and focusing ... (둘 다 동명사).

questions.passage: Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that __________ (respect) their past as an important part of who they are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: respect → respects. 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 단수 a way이므로 동사도 단수형 respects가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: respect → respects. 'in a way that __________ their past'에서 that은 앞의 단수 명사 a way를 가리키는 관계대명사이다. 선행사가 단수이므로 관계사절 안의 동사도 3인칭 단수형 respects가 필요하다.
det.tip: 관계대명사 주격: 선행사(a way, 단수)에 동사 수를 맞춰 respects.

questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is __________. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 친숙한 모든 것이 taken away(빼앗길) 때 아이들은 혼란을 느낀다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① taken away(빼앗기다/치워지다): 친숙한 모든 것이 사라질 때 혼란을 느낀다는 흐름에 맞는다.
❌ ② given back(돌려받다): 친숙한 것을 '돌려받으면' 혼란과 모순된다.
❌ ③ left alone(그대로 두다): 친숙한 것이 그대로 있으면 혼란이 없다.
❌ ④ set aside(제쳐두다): 문맥의 '사라지다'와 정확히 맞지 않는다.
det.tip: be taken away = 빼앗기다/치워지다.

questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's __________ and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 아이들의 past experiences(과거 경험)를 인정하는 것과 적응을 돕는 것 사이의 균형.
det.analysis:
❌ ① future plans(미래 계획): 인정(validating)의 대상은 미래가 아니라 과거이다.
✅ ② past experiences(과거 경험): 아이들의 과거 경험을 인정하는 것이 적응 돕기와 균형을 이룬다는 흐름에 맞는다.
❌ ③ daily routines(일상): 인정의 대상으로 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
❌ ④ new friends(새 친구): 문맥과 무관하다.
det.tip: validating children's past experiences = 아이들의 과거 경험을 인정하기.
